root_causes.title: `override` and `private` functions were invisible as scopes.
body: They are deliberately not reachability targets, so they are not collected -
but the reference map also used them to decide which scope a line sits in. A
call inside an `override` or `private` body was attributed to the nearest
preceding tracked declaration and then discarded as a self-reference.
Fix: `collect_scope_ranges` records brace-depth ranges for every class AND
function, including the untracked ones, and a line is attributed to the

root_causes.title: Line proximity cannot model nesting.
body: function `attemptDelivery`, so "nearest preceding declaration" picked the
inner class for lines the function actually contains.

root_causes.title: A class whose opening brace is on a later line was dropped.

stack and every fqcn inside it lost the class name. That turned live calls
into apparent external callers and mis-scored whole classes.

self_detection_note:
Self-detection also had to stop comparing names alone. An anonymous
`object : Callback { override fun onStartSuccess() }` computes the same
qualified name as the outer method it delegates to, so `this@Outer.m()` would
look recursive. The scope's start line is compared instead.

No flagged symbol is an `override`, an implemented interface member, an `@EntryPoint` accessor, or a serialization hook - so none of them qualifies for a detector exemption. Every exemption route was available and none was needed. The false-positive table above is the per-finding proof, re-derived on each run.

The detector scans `android/app/src/main` only. `android/shared/` and `shared/` are outside the corpus. Checked explicitly: none of the 32 findings was referenced from those roots. Recorded as a known limitation rather than silently ignored.
